headline: Highest risk is medium: Plane can ingest files and egress broadly, creating leakage and cascade risks when paired with a non-writing, non-networked collection agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between awesome-python and Plane, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. Plane can ingest file uploads and hyperlinks, while awesome-python is a non-runnable collection repo; any injection would require an unusual manual bridge such as copy-paste or uploaded content. The pathway is plausible but small.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from awesome-python into Plane file uploads or notes
IF Plane treats uploaded text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Avoid copying untrusted text between the two agents
Use a separate review step for any pasted content
Disable or restrict file uploads in Plane for this workflow
Tag imported content as untrusted in the operator process

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, notes, issues, and hyperlinks and has broad network egress, so sensitive workspace content could leave the environment by default. awesome-python itself has no data classes touched and no egress, but pairing it with Plane creates a shared-workflow leakage path if repository content or notes are moved into Plane. The blast radius includes multiple work products.
conditions: IF repository content from awesome-python is uploaded into Plane
IF Plane forwards notes, files, or issue text to external services over broad egress
mitigations: Keep sensitive material out of Plane uploads
Use a redaction pass before transferring content
Restrict Plane network access at the deployment boundary
Store only pointers, not file contents, in Plane
Review outbound integrations before enabling them

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write or network capabilities and Plane explicitly lacks filesystem write, so there is no meaningful write-write conflict. Plane supports multiple instances, which reduces contention further. Any overlap is limited to read-only coordination, so the pair does not present a serious capability conflict.
conditions: IF Plane is deployed with an external shared mutable resource not shown in the profile
IF another orchestrator grants filesystem write beyond the documented profile
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate resources
Avoid shared writable directories
Do not grant Plane extra filesystem permissions
Use instance-level separation for concurrent runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can act on issues, tasks, and notes, so if it consumes content derived from awesome-python, it may treat that content as authoritative without a verification step. awesome-python is a curated collection source, not a runnable verifier, so errors can cascade into Plane work items or decisions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF content from awesome-python is imported into Plane as tasks or issues
IF Plane users act on imported content without manual verification
mitigations: Require human verification before creating Plane tasks
Mark imported items as unverified
Separate source collection from action-taking workflows
Add a checklist step before any Plane issue is accepted

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and awesome-python touches no regulated data classes. Plane does handle files and notes, so compliance risk exists only if operators place regulated data into Plane. Because the other agent is not a data processor here, only Plane is relevant to the compliance pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Plane
IF Plane retention or export settings differ from the operator's policy
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in Plane
Check retention settings before use
Limit uploads to non-sensitive artifacts
Document a deletion/export process for Plane data
